angle: Your AI roadmap is gated by watts, cooling, and supply—treat facilities and procurement as first-class levers of ROI.
sourceTitle: Building the materials foundation for AI
linkedinPost:
Your AI strategy is probably constrained by physics, not models.

MIT Technology Review highlights the “materials foundation” behind AI—power, thermal management, reliability. We feel this daily: the blocker to scaling an agent isn’t prompt quality; it’s the data center row that’s out of power and the lead time on cooling.

My take: put Facilities and Procurement at the AI table. Model the ROI in watts: dollars per watt provisioned, cost-to-serve per interaction, and watts per business outcome (tickets resolved, orders taken).

Pragmatics that helped: prioritize use cases with high value per GPU-hour, invest in caching and off-peak batch where latency tolerates it, and negotiate power/cooling upgrades as part of the AI portfolio, not a back-office line item.

Also, build a “capacity runway” view—quarter-by-quarter visibility into power, cooling, and hardware supply. It prevents the classic stall where pilots win but production can’t scale.

If you track model metrics but not watts per outcome, you’re managing half the P&L.

What’s your biggest non-model constraint to scaling AI this year? #AIStrategy #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI
